sources.title: OCPP 2.0.1 Edition 4 Part 2 Specification with errata 2026-06

assertions.assertion: A secure UpdateFirmware always carries the provider's signing certificate and signature; the bridge verifies the certificate under the manufacturer root before sending, and an independent station validates the certificate before accepting and answers InvalidCertificate for an untrusted one.

A non-secure UpdateFirmware sends the provider location, retrieveDateTime, optional installDateTime, retries and retryInterval without any signing material; the reply is an acceptance, never proof of installation.

Every FirmwareStatusNotification of an update carries the requestId of the UpdateFirmwareRequest that started it; only Idle may omit it, and a notification without requestId for any other status is refused rather than attributed by guesswork.

The station reports every state it enters: DownloadScheduled for a future retrieval, Downloading per attempt and DownloadFailed after the last retry, InstallScheduled for a future install, InstallRebooting before the reboot and Installed from the activated firmware; the CSMS commits each status before its empty reply and progress never regresses.

After download the station verifies the request's signature over the entire received file using the signing certificate (RSA-PSS with SHA-256 from the test CA) and reports SignatureVerified or InvalidSignature; a configured verification fault reports InstallVerificationFailed.

A new UpdateFirmware while an update is pending cancels it with AcceptedCanceled, or is answered Rejected by a station unable to cancel; the CSMS marks the older job cancelled only on AcceptedCanceled and never treats Rejected as success.
A triggered FirmwareStatusNotification reports Idle after Installed (or with no update), otherwise the last sent status with its requestId.

Station firmware progress and the CSMS job survive a process kill and restart: an interrupted download is retried, an undelivered status is delivered once, a reboot is followed by Installed from the new firmware, and the CSMS never replays the request.
